subject: Origen AI — Dedicated capacity onboarding: kickoff, regions & burst policy
messages:
From: Lina Ortiz <lina@origen.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-10-28T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Kickoff: Origen Dedicated capacity + autoscale

Hi Evelyn / Ben,

Thanks again for the demo earlier this week — the team at Origen is excited to move forward with a dedicated GPU pool for our inference workloads. We have a target go-live window in mid-Jan 2028 (around 2028-01-15) and want to lock down region selection, autoscale/burst behavior, and an initial activation checklist so internal stakeholders can align procurement and infra changes.

High-level asks from our side: 
- Confirm recommended primary region (we prefer a US region with EU failover).
- Example autoscale/burst parameters (min capacity, burst QPS, cooldown windows).
- A simple activation checklist we can attach to our SRE runbook.
- Any dependencies for private VPC vs. hosted (we are leaning hosted to start).

Procurement will be included on follow-ups — Paul Morris (cc) will handle contract and PO timing. Can you share available times for a 45-min kickoff next week?

Best,
Lina Ortiz
Head of Platform, Origen AI
--
Origen AI
lina@origen.ai

Date: 2027-10-29T11:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Kickoff: Origen Dedicated capacity + autoscale

Lina — thanks, excited to partner on this. Quick reply with next steps and attachments.

Proposed next steps (45-min kickoff):
- Introductions & goals (10m)
- Traffic profile & SLOs (15m)
- Recommended region + burst/autoscale defaults (10m)
- Action items & timeline (10m)

Suggested default configuration to discuss:
- Primary region: us-west-2 (low latency to your US fleet)
- Failover region: eu-west-1 (for GDPR-covered traffic)
- Min reserved capacity: 4 GPUs (baseline)
- Autoscale: rule-based with target 70% GPU utilization, scale step 2 GPUs, cooldown 5m
- Burst policy: allow up to +3 GPUs (ephemeral burst) for 10 minutes per 5m window; burst governed by pool credit budget

Attachments I’m sending: onboarding_timeline_v1.pdf (timeline & milestones) and dedicated-activation-checklist.xlsx (activation artifacts).

Available times for kickoff: Tue 2027-11-02 09:00-11:00 PT or Wed 2027-11-03 13:00-15:00 PT. Evelyn, want to add anything on the implementation side?

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Thanks Ben — those defaults look reasonable. A few clarifying items from procurement and infra: 

1) Procurement: Paul here — can you confirm what the billing cadence & invoice process will look like for a reserved capacity + burst credits model? Also we may need a 60-day SOW review window.

2) Security/Deployment: our infra team asked whether the hosted model will expose audit logs and token-level traces (we need this for compliance). If hosted doesn't fully meet our needs, we may request a private control plane.

3) Burst policy detail: instead of raw GPU counts, can you provide a sample QPS-to-GPU mapping (we run a mix of short text-generation and embedding jobs)? Also, what is the fallback model if burst capacity is exhausted?

We can do Tue 2027-11-02 10:00 PT for the kickoff.

- Lina

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>
To: Lina Ortiz <lina@origen.ai>, Paul Morris <paul.morris@origen.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-11-01T09:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Kickoff: Origen Dedicated capacity + autoscale

Lina / Paul — thanks for the questions. Short answers + a technical appendix below. I’ve also attached a lightweight capacity estimate for your traffic (capacity-estimates.csv).

Billing & SOW: Billing is monthly for reserved capacity; burst credits are billed monthly on usage. We can accommodate a 60-day SOW review and will produce an SOW draft before procurement signs. Ben will follow up with contractual language.

Hosted auditability: Hosted mode includes token-level cost/latency breakdowns and request traces in the Console for the most recent 90 days. For customers requiring longer retention or customer-managed keys we recommend Redwood Private (VPC + private control plane). If you choose hosted for faster time-to-value, we can provide an interim audit export process to push logs to your S3 for 180-day retention.

Burst and fallback mapping (quick guidance):
- Example mapping (approx): 100 concurrent short-generation QPS ≈ 1 GPU (quantized model path); 250 QPS of embedding-requests ≈ 1 GPU. Map based on median token length and batching.
- Fallback: when burst capacity is depleted, requests will (in order of policy) 1) queue for up to 15s if ephemeral latency allowed, 2) route to a lower-cost quantized model variant in the same region, 3) route to failover region if latency SLO allows, 4) return 429 with backoff suggestion.

Implementation notes (for kickoff agenda):
- Prefix/KV caching: enable for chat workloads to keep token cost down.
- Autoscale policy: set target utilization at 65-75% for predictable tail latency.
- Throttles and billing: set a soft throttling policy for non-critical endpoints to preserve burst credits for production traffic.

Action items before kickoff (EOD 2027-11-01):
- Origen: share 2 sample production traces and 1 representative traffic CSV.
- Origen procurement: share preferred PO terms & contact (Paul).
- Redwood: draft SOW + high-level Mx plan (Ben) and produce capacity estimate (attached).

On the kickoff we’ll confirm the go/no-go criteria for hosted vs private.

Thanks,
Evelyn Hart
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
--
Attachments: capacity-estimates.csv (text/csv)
